setup.why: route takes the INTEGER plan id; need to resolve TP-1621 (__readonly__ plan) to its integer id via the project's plan listing

notes:
PASS on function: single attempt, 200, correct shape, owner/assignee present as declared. DRIFT on contract completeness: response includes test_plan.test_plan_progress and test_plan.test_results_trend, neither of which is listed in the capability's declared `returns` array (both are mentioned only in prose guidance, which says test_plan_progress is always {} and the real rollup is test_plan_progress_v2 — guidance is accurate, but the formal returns/schema enumeration omits both fields; a schema consumer relying only on `returns` would not know these keys exist). declared_missing (parent_plan, reviewers) are NOT contract violations: this is a top-level plan (parent_plan is sub-plan-only per guidance) with no review workflow configured (reviewers is conditional per guidance) — both absences are the documented, expected behavior, listed here only because the task requires the shallowest missing path. Also observed: test_plan_progress_v2 and test_results_trend_v2 came back as literal null (not {} / not an object) for this 0-test-run plan; the describeCapability 200 schema for this route does not type-expand these fields at all (only test_plan.identifier/name are given nested types), so this is not verifiable as a declared-type mismatch, just a live observation worth flagging for anyone assuming these are always objects.

SPECIFIC INTEREST — owner claim: CONFIRMED, holds live. get_test_plan_by_integer_id_v1 declares `owner` (and `assignee`, `created_by`, `completed_by`) in its `returns` list and the live 200 response for TP-1621 (integer id 48300) actually contains "owner": 2522 and a resolved "assignee" object. get_test_plan_v2's declared `returns` list has NO `owner` (and no `assignee`) — confirmed by re-reading its full expanded schema, which enumerates test_plan's properties in detail (identifier, name, description, active_state, tags, issues, test_runs_count, test_runs, sub_plans_count, parent_plan_id, start_date, end_date, created_at, project_id, links, urls) with no owner field anywhere. Live invocation of get_test_plan_v2 for the SAME plan (PR-2005/TP-1621) returned 200 with a test_plan object that indeed has no owner and no assignee key at all. So the routing eval's justification is correct on both counts: v1 (by integer id) returns owner, v2 does not — verified live, not just from contracts. If a caller asks 'who owns this plan', v2 alone cannot answer it; v1 is the right (currently only) capability that surfaces owner directly on a single-plan read.
